concepts.def: Group within wider society sharing distinctive values, norms and styles; e.g. punks, skinheads, emos.
Cohen (1955): working-class boys denied middle-class status form delinquent subcultures with inverted values.
Cloward and Ohlin (1960): blocked opportunities lead to criminal, conflict or retreatist subcultures depending on local conditions.
Hebdige (1979) Subculture: punk style as semiotic resistance using bricolage of safety pins, tartan, swastikas.
Maffesoli (1996) 'neo-tribes': youth identities fluid, consumer-based and short-lived rather than fixed subcultures.
Cohen (1972) studied Mods and Rockers; media amplification created exaggerated public reaction to youth subcultures.
